overall_summary: The performance data shows extremely low views and engagement across all 7 videos, likely due to a fresh channel or low distribution sample size. Because the sample size is very small and view counts are minimal (ranging from 3 to 20 views), confidence in statistical patterns is low. However, looking at slight relative variations, 'रिश्ते' and 'बेवफाई' topics with tangible phone/contact-related hooks performed slightly better than abstract late-night concepts.

winning_patterns.pattern: Tangible contact and mobile screen references
winning_patterns.evidence: Video A_eLARoegnw ('आज भी फोन में तुम्हारा नाम सुरक्षित है') got 20 views, the highest in the batch.
winning_patterns.action: Incorporate everyday smartphone micro-habits and digital memories into hooks.

weak_patterns.evidence: Video WhJ-VwRa3Rg ('घंटों से वो ऑनलाइन दिख रहा है।') received only 3 views.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid generic observation hooks and ground the opening in a specific physical or digital action.

next_video.concept: A short narrative about finding an old metro card or receipt with a date written on the back, reminding the protagonist of the last journey taken together.
next_video.opening_direction: Purane bill ya ticket ke peeche aaj bhi woh tareekh likhi hai...
next_video.twist_direction: ...aur sapne mein lagta hai ki woh safar abhi khatam nahi hua, bas ticket return ho gayi.
next_video.reason: Testing a shift from digital/phone screens to tangible offline objects to see if tactile nostalgia triggers better retention than chat/online status themes.

experiment: Testing an offline physical artifact (old ticket/receipt) instead of smartphone screen habits to measure if tactile memory hooks improve engagement.
